key_insight: Bayesian inference combined with photoluminescence imaging and drift-diffusion modeling can localize where perovskite solar cells degrade, separating interface-driven damage from bulk effects.
engineering_relevance: The approach helps engineers diagnose failure mechanisms in real devices and guides targeted passivation or interface design to improve long-term stability.
method: Photoluminescence imaging of fully fabricated perovskite solar cells
Drift-diffusion simulations linked to measured optical data
Bayesian inference to generate spatial parameter maps and track them during aging
evidence_signal: The authors aged devices at 70 °C under full-spectrum sunlight and observed spatially non-uniform parameter-map changes, with the strongest degradation concentrated at perovskite/transport-layer interfaces.
watch_item: The inferred maps depend on model assumptions and measurement quality, so inaccurate drift-diffusion or prior settings could bias the localization of degradation.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
